events.text: Air support for Kesselwand rescues is provided by Alpenflug, flying from the Talheim heliport.
The primary team radio channel is VHF channel 4.
The avalanche dog unit works on VHF channel 7.
The Rotstein refuge hut gets its heating fuel from Huber Brennstoffe.
The Schneekar bivouac hut gets its heating fuel from Kramer Energie.
Weekday standby shifts at the Kesselwand base start at 07:00.
Weekend standby shifts at the Kesselwand base start at 06:00.
Team ropes are inspected every 6 months.
Callouts to the Hollenzahn north face stage from the Moosalm car park.
The team's medical director is Dr. Ilse Brandner.
Team members carry Lumis T2 avalanche transceivers.
The standard casualty stretcher is the Brenner folding litter.
Members are alerted to callouts by SMS pager through the regional dispatch centre.
Team training night is on Tuesday evenings.
The monthly kit check happens on the first Wednesday of the month.
Glacier approaches must be roped whenever the party has fewer than four members.
Air support for Kesselwand rescues moved to Bergair, still flying from the Talheim heliport, after the 2024 contract tender.
The primary team radio channel changed to VHF channel 7 after interference from the ski resort's lift radios.
The Schneekar bivouac hut switched its heating fuel supplier to Huber Brennstoffe.
Team ropes are inspected every 3 months; the earlier 6-month figure was a typo in the handbook.
Callouts to the Hollenzahn north face now stage from the Lindenhof car park after the Moosalm road closed.
The standard casualty stretcher changed to the Velta split litter for helicopter compatibility.
Team training night moved to Wednesday evenings to avoid clashing with the ski club.
The primary team radio channel changed to digital talkgroup TG-31 when the TETRA network went live in 2024.
Air support for Kesselwand rescues went back to Alpenflug, now flying from the Grauberg airfield, after Bergair lost its night-flying licence in 2025.
Weekend standby shifts at the Kesselwand base now start at 07:00 since the summer 2025 rota review.
The monthly kit check moved to the first Tuesday of the month after the autumn 2025 rota change.
The Rotstein refuge hut switched its heating fuel supplier to Kramer Energie in 2025.
Team members now carry Lumis T4 avalanche transceivers, issued in winter 2025.
The avalanche dog unit moved to digital talkgroup TG-35 in the summer 2026 re-banding so handlers can hear the main team.
The primary team radio channel changed to digital talkgroup TG-35 in the summer 2026 re-banding.
The Schneekar bivouac hut switched its heating fuel supplier to Weiss Gas after Huber stopped delivering above 2000 metres.
The standard casualty stretcher changed to the Aurus vacuum mattress litter in autumn 2025.
Weekday standby shifts at the Kesselwand base now start at 06:30 to cover early climbers.
Air support for Kesselwand rescues has been provided by Nordlicht Aviation from the Grauberg airfield since the spring 2026 handover.
Members are now alerted to callouts through the AlpAlarm smartphone app instead of SMS pagers, since March 2026.
Team ropes are now inspected every 2 months under the 2026 equipment standard.
Team training night moved to Thursday evenings in January 2026.
The primary team radio channel changed to digital talkgroup TG-38 after the September 2026 network audit.
The primary team radio channel for the regional drill changed to digital talkgroup TG-40, replacing TG-38.
Air support for rescues switched from Nordlicht Aviation to Bergair in the autumn 2026 tender.
